newsitem.title: USA: Varlen sees positive quarterly comparisons.
newsitem.headline: Varlen sees positive quarterly comparisons.

text.p: Varlen Corp, which makes transportation products for the railroad, truck and automotive industries, said Tuesday it expects to post positive quarter-to-quarter comparisons for the rest of 1997.

"We have a number of reasons for believing Varlen should post positive quarter-to-quarter comparisons for the rest of 1997," Richard Wellek, chairman, said in a statement. "All four of our operations are seeing positive industry trends."
The company also said that favorable comparisons to prior year results could occur in the second half, which would lead to a record year.
In June, Varlen said it expected record sales and earnings for fiscal 1997. In fiscal 1996, it earned $2.04 a share, including a $0.23 gain for the sale of a business.
Commenting on the outlook, Wellek said industry experts believe the second-half railcar build rate could exceed the first, and freightcar backlogs are at their highest level in nine months.

"Orders for Class 8 (heavy-duty) trucks have exceeded production for the last 10 months, and most manufacturers are increasing their production rates," Wellek said. "Sales of light trucks, where Varlen's automotive operation has its highest content per vehicle, continue to grow. Petroleum analyzer sales should benefit from seasonal factors, rising oil company profits, and new products."

Earlier, Varlen reported earnings for the second quarter ended August 2 of $0.66 a share, down from year-ago earnings of $0.73 a share, which included a $0.23 gain for the sale of a business. Excluding the gain, net earnings for the second quarter rose by 42.5 percent.
"Sales for our railroad products business nearly doubled between the two second quarter," Wellek said.

The heavy-duty truck/trailer business saw a 27 percent sales increase, and the automotive products business increased its sales eight percent despite labor disruptions at General Motors Corp and Chrysler Corp, Varlen said.
Analytical instruments sales were up 22 percent during the quarter, excluding sales from a business sold in 1996.
